correctness.rationale: All LD-set omission constraints are derived from actual open-neighborhood signatures. The proof shows that three coalition partners would force their common block to be LD; hence four or more blocks require disjoint coalition pairs. Disjointness forces original part sizes at most two and at most two singleton parts; a fifth block forces an LD singleton partner contradiction. Explicit three- and four-block constructions prove sharpness. Direct exhaustive independently implemented verification matches all 86 multipartite order profiles through nine vertices.

value.rationale: A complete exact answer is obtained for a natural unrestricted infinite family and the recently introduced LDC parameter. The part-size rigidity yields a size-independent four-block ceiling, sharper than the generic bound by an unbounded amount on graphs with many two-vertex parts. The two/three/four part-size boundary is structurally informative, not a small arithmetic special case.
